question.text: Per the current NISM VIII workbook (current NIFTY options contract specifications, lot size 50), what is the total premium outflow for buying 10 lots of NIFTY 25,000 call options at Rs 300 per unit?

answer.text: Rs 1,50,000 (300 × 50 × 10, using current NIFTY options lot size of 50)

explanation.text: The Logic: Premium per lot = Premium per unit × Lot size. Using the current NIFTY options contract size of 50: Premium per lot = 300 × 50 = Rs 15,000. Total for 10 lots = 15,000 × 10 = Rs 1,50,000. This is the maximum loss (premium paid) for the option buyer. The Trap: The legacy NIFTY lot size of 25 would give Rs 75,000, but the current workbook specifications use a higher lot size. Rs 3,000 ignores lot size entirely; Rs 30,000 uses an incorrect 100 per lot. Cross-Exam Context: NISM VIII tests current contract specifications and emphasises that lot sizes are exchange-determined and revised from time to time; always confirm the current lot size before computing premium outflow.
